words: لا تضار والدة بولدها ولا مولود له بولده
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared form can mean either spouse harms the other through the child; Samarrai says it deliberately covers both directions and prevents either from causing harm.
rows.anchor: فأراد تعالى المعنيين لكيلا يقع الضرر من أحدهما على الآخر فجاء بصيغة تدل على المعنيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an chooses the highest expression suited to the intended meaning and context; Samarrai identifies this precision as its inimitability against Arab eloquence.
rows.anchor: ولقد تفرّد القرآن الكريم باختيار التعبير الأعلى في المعنى المُراد وفي المكان الذي يقتضيه هذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The non-Qur’anic example distinguishes a verbal noun that means only the act of giving from ʿaṭāʾ, which can mean either good giving or a good gift/wealth.
rows.anchor: أما العطاء فهو اسم المصدر بمعنى الإعطاء أو المال والعطاء يحتمل معنيين إعطاء حسن ومال حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samarrai describes the episode as exceptionally strange: about 600 men in a fortress surrendered their weapons without fighting, then lost their homes, property, and families.
rows.anchor: كانوا 600 رجل في الحصن ألقوا أسلحتهم من غير قتال وكانوا في حالة رعب عجيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The killed group is fronted because killing was the most astonishing outcome of the terror; the captured group is not fronted because it consisted of women and children, with no fighters to kill.
rows.anchor: أما مع الأسر فلا داعي هنا لتقديم (فريقاً) على (تأسرون) لأنه ليس هناك مقاتلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative names Iblis because he is the father of devils just as Adam is father of humanity, marking the original conflict between their forebears.
rows.anchor: إبليس هو أبو الشياطين كما إن آدم أبو البشر وبداية الصراع كان بين أبو البشر وأبو الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samarrai says shayṭān can denote any unbelieving jinn, including an individual unbeliever among the jinn.
rows.anchor: والشيطان يُطلق على كل من كان كافراً من الجن أي على الفرد الكافر من الجنّ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Adam story in al-Aʿrāf sits amid punishment, destruction of wrongdoers, and rebuke for ingratitude and heedlessness.
rows.anchor: سياق القصة في سورة الأعراف ورد في العقوبات وإهلاك الأمم الظالمة من بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqara alone gathers Iblis’s refusal, arrogance, and unbelief to stress the enormity of his sin; al-Aʿrāf instead mentions only that he was not among those prostrating.
rows.anchor: وهذه الصفات لم تأت مجتمعة إلا في سورة البقرة لبيان شناعة معصية إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing Adam’s instruction directly to God in Baqara marks honor; in al-Aʿrāf the command follows the joint address that expels Iblis.
rows.anchor: الملاحظ في القرآن أنه لما ينسب الله تعالى القول إلى ذاته يكون في مقام التكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqara says God accepted Adam’s repentance without recounting his request, fitting its honoring tone; al-Aʿrāf recounts Adam’s plea but not God’s acceptance.
rows.anchor: ذكر في البقرة أن الله تعالى تاب على آدم ولم يذكر أن آدم طلب المغفرة لكن وردت التوبة والمغفرة عليه وهذا مناسب لجو التكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿrāf contrasts the angels, who do not act arrogantly and do prostrate, with Iblis, who neither prostrates nor may be arrogant.
rows.anchor: نفى تعالى عن الملائكة التكبر وأكدّ سجودهم ولكن بالنسبة لإبليس في السورة نفسها نفى عنه السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s prediction that most people would not be grateful comes true: the sūra first notes humanity’s provision and establishment in the land, then records his prediction.
rows.anchor: فصدّق عليهم إبليس ظنّه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general command in Baqara is addressed to the angels, while Iblis received a separate, specific command in al-Aʿrāf; he need not be counted among the angels commanded there.
rows.anchor: فليس بالضرورة أن الله تعالى أمر إبليس بالسجود مع الملائكة لكنه تعالى أمر الملائكة بالسجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samarrai says a masculine verb with a broken plural signals a small group, as with the few women in Joseph’s story; a feminine verb can signal a larger group, as with the many Arab tribes.
rows.anchor: تذكير الفعل يستعمل مع جمع التكسير ليفيد القلة كما جاء في الآية في سورة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An oath’s answer is stated when the purpose calls for it; elsewhere it can be omitted because context supplies it or to leave the meaning open.
rows.anchor: جواب القسم ليس بالضرورة أن يُذكر بحسب الغرض منه فإذا اقتضى أن يُجاب القسم يُجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Qāf and Ṣād the oath response is omitted so the meaning can encompass whatever the surrounding verses suggest, rather than fixing one response.
rows.anchor: فلا يريد تعالى جواباً بعينه لكنه يريد أن يوسع المعنى

rows.speaker: قسم من المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators identify qad aflaḥa man zakkāhā as the answer to the oath in Sūrat al-Shams.
rows.anchor: وقسم من المفسرين قال في سورة الشمس أن جواب القسم هو (قد أفلح من زكاها)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In wa-in taʿuddū niʿmata Allāh, the singular is generic: it means the whole category of divine favors, not one favor.
rows.anchor: النعمة هنا ليست مفردة وإنما هي جنس النعمة وليست مفردة واحدة وإنما هي عامة تشمل كل النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis was commanded separately as well as the angels collectively: the author reads the angels’ general order in Baqara and a specific order to Iblis in al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: وأمر إبليس بالسجود أمراً خاصاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and almsgiving were commanded in earlier religions, whereas pilgrimage is distinctively Islamic; inviting people to pilgrimage thus amounts to inviting them to Islam, unlike calling them to practices they already observe.
rows.anchor: الصلاة والزكاة كان مأمور بهما من تقدّم من أهل الديانات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Aʿrāf, lā is emphatic and nonnegative: reading it as negation would make God reproach Iblis for prostrating, while the charge is his failure to prostrate; Ṭā Hā uses a similar construction.
rows.anchor: إذن (لا) مزيدة للتوكيد جيء بها لغرض التوكيد لأن المعلوم أن يحاسبه على عدم السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb is called the brother of Midian because he belonged to them; the People of al-Aykah were not his kin, so their account names him without brotherhood.
rows.anchor: وأصحاب الأيكة ولم يكن منهم وليسوا من أهله فلم يذكر معهم أخوهم شعيب لأنه ليس أخوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus addresses the Israelites as Children of Israel rather than my people because he is not genealogically one of them; Moses uses my people because he is.
rows.anchor: يخاطبهم بـ (بني إسرائيل) لأنه ليس له نسب فيهم أما في قصة موسى فالخطاب على لسان موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samarrai says the Qur’an always uses lā uqsimu, never bare aqsimu: lā confirms the oath, can magnify an already evident object, and sometimes intensifies the oath.
rows.anchor: لم يرد في القرآن كله كلمة (أقسم) أبداً وإنما استخدم لفظ (لا أقسم) بمعنى أقسم و (لا) لتأكيد القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lā may be an emphatic connective when ambiguity is impossible; al-Aʿrāf’s rebuking context and frequent prostration support its use in this question.
rows.anchor: هناك قاعدة (لا) يمكن أن تُزاد إذا أُمن اللبس، وسُمّيت حرف صلة وغرضها التوكيد وليس النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿrāf has more emphatic forms, a longer Adam account, and more prostration-root forms than Ṣād; Samarrai says this context makes the added lā fitting.
rows.anchor: ثم إن مشتقات السجود في سورة الأعراف أكثر (9 مرات) أما في سورة ص (3 مرات)

rows.speaker: القدامى
rows.claim: Earlier scholars observed that the disconnected opening letters stamp a sūra with a characteristic letter pattern, reflected in its vocabulary.
rows.anchor: انتبه له القدامى في السور التي تبدأ بالأحرف المقطعة وهي أن هذه الأحرف تطبع السورة بطابعها

rows.speaker: جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr counted the sequence alif-lām-rāʾ 220 times in its sūra.
rows.anchor: جعفر بن الزبير أحصى ورود الر 220 مرة في السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because al-Aʿrāf opens with alif-lām-mīm-ṣād and the added lā uses lām and alif, Samarrai finds the wording suited to the sūra’s opening letters as well as its context.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية موضع السؤال اللام والألف وهما أحرف (لا) فناسب ذكر (لا) في آية سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a usage correction, Samarrai says one should say I apologize for not attending, not I apologize for attending.
rows.anchor: مثلاً من الخطأ الشائع أننا نقول أعتذر عن الحضور وإنما الصحيح القول: أعتذر عن عدم الحضور.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqara adds rag̱adan, a detail Samarrai considers fitting to that sūra’s honoring tone; al-Aʿrāf omits it.
rows.anchor: المناسب للتكريم في السورة بينما لم ترد في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqara’s wāw joins dwelling and eating without fixing sequence, allowing unbounded choice; al-Aʿrāf’s fa orders eating immediately after dwelling. Wāw can indicate order but is not limited to it.
rows.anchor: لا مانع أن تأتي الواو للترتيب لكن لا تُحصر للترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Baqara, ḥaythu shiʾtumā can govern both dwelling and eating, widening Adam’s choices; in al-Aʿrāf, min ḥaythu shiʾtumā concerns only where they eat, matching the narrower fa.
rows.anchor: في سورة البقرة تحتمل أن تكون للسكن والأكل؛ بمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqara’s azallahumā can mean a slip without descent and softens the lapse in an honoring context; al-Aʿrāf’s dallāhumā explicitly lowers them, fitting its punitive context.
rows.anchor: والتدلية لا تكون إلا من أعلى لأسفل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 7:26, clothing that veils physical nakedness suits outward covering, while the garment of piety veils inward faults; the image follows the temptation to expose Adam and his wife.
rows.anchor: اختار تعالى للتقوى كلمة اللباس الذي يواري السوءات الباطنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clothing and piety passage is a warning from God to Adam’s descendants.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآيات تحذير من الله تعالى لذرية آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭūr adds kāhin because disbelievers broadened their accusations against the Prophet; its references to seers and magic also suit that addition, unlike al-Qalam’s briefer wording.
rows.anchor: توسّع الكافرون في التُّهم لذا استدعى السياق إدخال كلمة (كاهن) كزيادة
